title: Maxmin And Minmax
body_html:
Maxmin And Minmax

Scope. This node is the abstract / pure-strategy version: $I$ and $J$ are arbitrary nonempty strategy sets, and the inner extremum ranges over pure strategies. The finite mixed-strategy instantiation (with $x \in \Delta(I)$, $y \in \Delta(J)$, and Mathlib's Finset.inf' / Finset.sup') lives in Maximin and Minimax Values and is the one currently formalised.

For a zero-sum game $(I,J,g)$, the maxmin is $$ \underline v = \sup_{i \in I} \inf_{j \in J} g(i,j), $$ and the minmax is $$ \overline v = \inf_{j \in J} \sup_{i \in I} g(i,j). $$ The maxmin is the best amount player 1 can guarantee, and the minmax is the least amount player 2 can guarantee as an upper bound on player 1's payoff.

References

  • [MFoGT, Def. 2.2.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Maxmin and minmax of a zero-sum game.
